indicators.note: the pair of pieces is set inside the name of the Chinese dynasty, splitting it after its first letter

parts.note: the Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644
the Roman numeral for one is I
ST, short for saint, is crossword shorthand for a good person

explanation.surface: A TV crew is shooting a costume drama, with one virtuous character in a historical saga.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'dynasty' point at a TV soap, but the word is a Chinese dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Misting means covering with a thin film of droplets, as a lens or window does, so it fits a cryptic reading of filming.

clue.text: Drivers' club caught by distance sign

indicators.note: the club's letters are caught and held within the word for a distance

parts.note: a mile is a unit of distance
the RAC, the Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: A motoring club spots a road sign showing the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is a British motorists' club, like the AA.
explanation.definitionFit: A miracle is a sign, a wonder showing divine power, as in the Gospels.

clue.text: Two points before the bird's never-ending class

annotationWithheld.why: Two points before the bird's never-ending class: SE plus a shortened bird should give MINAR, but no bird word less its last letter gives MINAR (MINAH gives only MINA), and no source has the clue's parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Two points before the bird's never-ending class

clue.text: Unfit after one new article on exercise

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so the first pieces stand over the exercise letters

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a is the indefinite article
PT is physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: Someone is unfit to take part after a new piece on exercise is published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfit' suggests poor physical condition, which the exercise in the clue supports; here it means unsuitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or inappropriate for the purpose.

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the next word are arranged in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Describes someone as both warm-hearted and oddly charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' reads as the adjective meaning friendly, but it is a sweet drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadine is a sweet syrup made from pomegranates, mixed into drinks as a cordial.

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of ship is used

parts.note: a kipper is a smoked herring

explanation.surface: Asks whether a ship's captain is the one transporting a cargo of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: S, the first letter of 'ship', sits in front of KIPPER (it carries the fish), and the whole clue describes a captain.
explanation.definitionFit: The captain of a vessel is commonly called its skipper, especially on a fishing boat.

explanation.surface: An exclamation alerting someone that a dangerous seductress is approaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a wailing alarm; in Greek myth the Sirens lured sailors to their doom with song, hence a seductive woman.

indicators.note: whacking something beats it out of shape, so the letters of the next word are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A headline announcing a huge price cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whacking' looks like 'huge' (a whacking reduction), but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To introduce a speaker or act is to present or announce them.

indicators.note: by means beside, so the word for finished off follows the word for puritanical

parts.note: prim means strait-laced or puritanical
ate means finished off food

explanation.surface: Someone was done in by a strait-laced senior cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A primate is an archbishop, the chief bishop of a province.

clue.text: Concerning a fellow that provokes a reaction

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
a gent is a gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: A remark about a man whose behaviour provokes a response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reaction' suggests someone's response, but it is a chemical reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a substance added to cause a chemical change.

clue.text: Frenzy of passion embracing a politician

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold something in the arms, so the word for passion wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: rage is a violent passion
MP, Member of Parliament, is a British politician

explanation.surface: A frenzied fit of passion during which someone hugs an elected representative.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe wild, uncontrolled behaviour, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Sit near buffet to find a drink

indicators.note: to buffet is to knock about, so the letters of the first two words are battered into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to sit close to the buffet table if you want to get a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' looks like a noun for a spread of food, but it is a verb meaning to batter, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
a strain is a type or variety, as of a plant or virus

explanation.surface: A command to lock up a certain kind of criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain someone is to confine or restrict them, which is what imprisoning does.

clue.text: Make a speech on zero tax

parts.note: the digit zero looks like the letter O
rates are a local British property tax, so a rate is a tax

explanation.surface: A politician gives a speech about abolishing a tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal address in a lofty style.

indicators.note: losing the head means the opening letter of the word for fiend is removed

parts.note: a terror is a fearsome person or fiend; the 's is short for 'is', linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A ghost story's headless demon turns out to be only a delusion.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'fiend' is 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistaken belief, and a delusion is a false belief.

parts.note: re means about or concerning
port is the left side of a ship
to age is to grow older and decline

explanation.surface: A news story covering the waning fortunes of the political left.
explanation.definitionFit: Reportage is the reporting of events in the press, journalism.

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rogue
saucy humour is rude
NT is the New Testament, a set of old books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Asks whether a scoundrel's risqué antique books are the work of a reckless man.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent means unwise or lacking caution, close to rash.

clue.text: Smooth hunk means to undo clothes?

parts.note: to press clothes is to smooth them with an iron
a stud is an attractive man, a hunk

explanation.surface: Asks whether a smooth, good-looking man has his way of getting clothes off.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests seduction; the definition is just a snap fastener, which undoes clothes when pulled apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A press stud is a snap fastener on garments, pulled apart to open them.

clue.text: Curse MP — he's able to change…

indicators.note: the letters of MP and he's able are to be changed into another order

explanation.surface: A Member of Parliament is said to be capable of swearing, the sentence trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses join this clue to 19-across, but the two are solved separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To blaspheme is to speak profanely of sacred things, to swear.

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the swimmer word takes the liberal letter inside it

parts.note: a bather is someone who floats in water
L is short for Liberal

explanation.surface: A drifting politician admits to the Liberal Party's waffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Blather is long-winded, empty talk.

parts.note: a bridge spans a gap, so it is a spanner

explanation.surface: Asks whether you can squeeze something tight with a wrench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spanner' looks like the wrench, but it is anything that spans, here a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten or condense it.

parts.note: to ease or moderate a pain is to lessen it

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so labour gives only its start

explanation.surface: Continuing 17-across: a moderate Labour Party leader's position on an issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour leader' suggests the head of Britain's Labour Party; here it is just the first letter of 'labour'.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand used to hold an artist's canvas.

indicators.note: over says the whole string of pieces is turned back to front

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry to have mailed something a second time once it was all done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the whole run, so S SEND AS read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadness is sorrow, and regret is sorrow over something done.

clue.text: Small insect in part of eye

indicators.note: the bug goes inside the part of the eye

parts.note: the lid closes over the eye
a mite is a tiny bug (strictly an arachnid)

explanation.surface: A tiny bug has got into someone's eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: Limited means restricted in size or amount.

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Someone frames a song performed by a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: An airer is a clothes horse, a frame for drying laundry.

clue.text: Where to find trams and Edam, possibly

definitions.text: Where to find trams and Edam, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the two words may come out in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Names the place where you would come across both trams and Edam cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dutch capital has a well-known tram network, and Edam is a cheese from a town nearby, so the whole clue is a description too.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch capital is famous for its trams and sells Edam cheese from nearby North Holland.

indicators.note: first places the word for state ahead of the other piece

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

indicators.note: the middle of the word eastern is its central letter

explanation.surface: A ruling to block a Middle Eastern country from coming first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle eastern' reads as Middle East; it is the middle letter of 'eastern'.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert a disaster is to ward it off before it happens.

indicators.note: say means the answer is heard rather than seen, so the word for samovars is spoken

parts.note: a samovar is a Russian tea urn

explanation.surface: Tea is drawn off from Russian samovars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draws' looks like drawing tea from a tap, but it means is paid, as in draws a salary.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a wage is to receive it, so earning money and drawing it are synonymous.

definitions.note: water is a verb here; the 's is short for 'is', linking to the wordplay

indicators.note: frothy liquid is churned up, so these letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Hard water still produces froth, a remark about soap and limescale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water's hard' reads as a remark about limescale; 'Water' is the verb meaning to give water.
explanation.definitionFit: To hydrate something is to supply it with moisture, as watering plants does.

indicators.note: the word for guys sits inside the legal word for a wrong

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men are guys

explanation.surface: Wrongly accused men find themselves in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To torment someone is to trouble or harass them persistently.

clue.text: Vote again for right slippery character — big shock

parts.note: an eel is a slippery fish, and a slippery person
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, a large electric shock

explanation.surface: A voter backs the right-wing candidate again, a devious type, to everyone's alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-elect someone is to choose them by ballot once more.

clue.text: Unemployed south American stopped working outside

indicators.note: the word for stopped working goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a machine that died stopped working
US means American, as in US troops

explanation.surface: A southern American man has lost his job because his workplace shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unemployed' suggests a jobless person, but here it means no longer in use.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disused is no longer put to use.
